Dans la rue 3D, les grands ponts de la l: In the 3D street, the lagoon's big bridges are drawn the way they are built, in blocks: the Félix-Houphouët-Boigny bridge with its railway level where you see the train go past through the openings, its blade piers and old balustrade; the Charles-de-Gaulle bridge with its girder deeper over the piers; the Henri-Konan-Bédié bridge, its two box girders side by side on round piers, its tall lamps down the middle and its footpath; the Alassane-Ouattara bridge, its leaning white pylon and its 19 stays lit at night. Railings, markings, joints, lamps lit in the evening: from afar at night, the bridges become strings of light over the lagoon. You drive and walk on them as before.
Dans la rue 3D, tous les véhicules sont: In the 3D street, every vehicle is rebuilt in detailed blocks: the orange taxi compteur becomes a real saloon with its « TAXI » roof sign and its number on the doors, the woro-woros keep their colour band, the gbaka has its sliding door open, its apprenti, its loaded roof rack and its motto painted on the back, the SITRA bus its lit destination sign, the motos their chrome forks. Every car you can buy keeps its model and its colour (saloon, 4×4 with bull bar and spare wheel, pick-up, limousine…). Clear-coated paint, windows that reflect the sky, number plates, dust on the sills, headlights and tail lights that come on at night, wheels that roll and steer. From afar, a simple, light version.

A few seconds each time, a bit of good mood, and you move on whenever you like.
Dans le chat de groupe (Tout Babi, ta co: In the group chat (All Babi, your commune), when you reply to an NPC or call them by name, they answer in their own words, like a real conversation. They pick up your way of writing: short or long, slang or proper, with emojis or not, in English if you write in English. And they do what you ask when words can do it: a joke, a story, a riddle, advice, a quiz, a made-up zouglou verse, a plan for tonight. Now and then they take up questions left unanswered in the chat. Public chat: nothing sexual, no flirting, no numbers or links.

Dans ton téléphone, l'appli « Voisins »: In your phone, the « Neighbours » app: the three families of your yard, always the same, with their name, their trade, their character and their children. Their life goes on with the days: a baby, a wedding, a new job, a quarrel heard through the wall, a family moving out and another moving in. They come and ask you: to lend a little money, to come to the baptism, to keep the children, to help put up the wardrobe, the music too loud in the middle of the night, condolences. Greet them, bring them a dish, answer yes or no: the bond goes up or down. Close, they bring you food and pay back what they borrowed. The date is played: they talk to you, you pick a sweet word, a joke or listening, and their face answers. Every morning, your other half writes « Good morning sweetheart ». Ton perso peut tomber malade, comme dans: Your character can fall ill, just like in real life: malaria (mosquitoes, at night), flu when worn out, typhoid or a stomach ache when hygiene slips, a sprain at sport. Ill, they tire faster and feel low; untreated, it gets worse each day. Pharmacy medicine treats a minor illness, a consultation at the health centre treats the rest. A treated mosquito net (at the pharmacy) keeps malaria away. And when an elder of the family passes away, you choose their funeral (simple, dignified or grand, with the band): the family chips in, the renown grows, and you watch the ceremony.
Ton perso vieillit pendant que tu joues: Your character ages while you play (never while the game is closed or paused): young adult, adult, senior. At 60, or from 50 with 3 of the 5 milestones met (owner, boss, fortune, respected, family), you hand over: your 18-year-old child, a child adopted at the orphanage, or else a nephew or niece takes over the house, the name, the lots, the buildings, the vehicles and your neighbourhood. The money passes after inheritance tax: three quarters to the heir, a quarter to the elder, who gives it back as weekly blessings. Debts never pass on. Diplomas and papers are the heir's own: they retake their BEPC and bac. They keep part of what you knew how to do, and your friends become their uncles and aunties. In an official couple with a player, you can have a child together, if they say yes: the first of you two to hand down to them takes them. With no child, your childhood friend's child can also take over the house. Your elders drop by the commune's grin, sit in front of your house in Mon quartier and come to your soirées. The elders stay at home: advice, a blessing, a visit; two generations later, they go off to rest in the village. Each generation adds to your family's renown: the « Ma famille » app shows the tree, the milestones, the elders and the ranking of the great families.
